hint.label: Vocabulary list

atoms.b: A person's ((sexual_orientation)) describes which genders somebody is or is not attracted to. The ((label)) homosexual (from Greek “homos” = “the same”) describes attraction towards members of the same gender, while those who feel attracted to a different gender than their own commonly ((identify)) as heterosexual (from Greek “heteros” = “different”).

In many Western countries, homosexuality was still forbidden until a few decades ago. The UK and the USA have only ((decriminalised decriminalized)) homosexual acts in the 1960s, and ((same-sex_marriage same_sex_marriage)) has only been legal in those countries since 2014 and 2015 respectively.

While people whose ((gender_identity)) aligns with the sex they were ((assigned)) at birth are called cisgender (from Latin “cis” = “on the same side”), those who do not identify with their ((biological_sex)) are referred to as being transgender (from Latin “trans” = “on the other side”).

Many people view gender as a rigid binary, only consisting of two poles with no variation in between. “Male” and “female” fall into these ((binary)) gender identities. However, gender is a broad spectrum with many more options. Those who do not ((conform)) to this binary are often called gender nonconforming.

Unfortunately, there is still a lot of violence and ((prejudice)) against queer people to this day. The term for this hatred and unfair treatment of homosexual individuals is homophobia, and for trans people it is ((transphobia)). This includes the ((reinforcement)) of harmful stereotypes, such as that queer people pose a danger to others, and the use of ((derogatory)) remarks.
